# Study X: which headline simulation results survive the corrected models (the re-baseline)

<!-- Written for the lead by study X. Numbers come from results/rebaseline/*.json (tables regenerated by
`python3 -m rebaseline.report` into rebaseline/build/doc_tables.md). Nothing here was built or measured. -->

## In plain words

*30 September 2026. Every number below is a SIMULATION (the model, the sensing mode and the inputs are named with
it), a CALCULATION, an ASSUMPTION or LITERATURE. Nothing in this programme has been built, and nothing was measured on
a pen or a person.*

**What changed.** The engineering pass of 30 September found that several simulations let the pen's controller know
more than a real pen could (the nib's exact speed, the true ball force, a contact flag with no delay, and a page
sensor whose error could look ahead and whose lost motion came back), ran an inner loop that is unstable once the
sensing is realistic, and under-counted the balanced nib's loads (wire tension against a stiff anchor, about 8 mN of
guide drag). DEC-070 suspended those results. This study went through all 69 simulation rows of the preserved claims
register (task 1: 29 rerun here, 23 unaffected, 15 affected but not rerun, each with its reason, 2 superseded by the
pass) and reran the affected ones on the current code, case by case on the same writers, cells and
seeds, after first checking that the old settings reproduce the published numbers (they do, exactly, once the old
firmware contact channel, which the pass replaced without a switch, is restored at run time).

**What survives.**
- **Rev J + G4 in the whole-pen simulator (synthetic tremor) survives causal sensing:** ink error 0.61 of the
  ordinary pen at 8–12 Hz × 1–2 mm (published 0.63), words read 7.5 → 10 of 10 (7.7 → 10), tremor-free writing
  untouched. The small "improvement" is not real: G4's own ink is unchanged and the comparison pen got slightly worse.
  The mild-tremor (1.01) and slow-tremor (1.00) cards are unchanged, and writing through 3 mm of tremor also
  survives (words 4 → 42 %, published 4 → 38 %). **Autowrite does not survive unchanged**: at 3 mm the C1S nose now writes 68 % of words instead of 88 %, about
  25 µm less accurately in every case (a bench-module mechanism result; in-pen autowrite is superseded by DEC-071).
- **Study F's reach answer survives the balanced nib's own servo and mass:** with perfect knowledge at the severe
  class (real inputs, tuning split), ±1.5 mm still gains +3.2 words of 10 (2.6 to 3.8) and clears DEC-055's +2 line;
  Rev K's ±1.06 mm gains +1.6 (0.7 to 2.4) and does not. The dynamics cost only 0.02 mm.
- **The real-input conclusions of studies R, E and F survive the causal page model:** no tracker helps at the
  severe class (words 0.1–0.4 of 10 against the ordinary pen's 0.5); E's frozen design still fails DEC-055; the
  estimators still leave about 1.1 mm.
- **The balanced nib's synthetic benefit survives DEC-066's 40/46 Hz servo, causal sensing and the corrected loads**
  (sim2, synthetic inputs, after reproducing study B's own rows exactly): G4 leaves 0.57 of the held nib's ink error
  on Rev K and 0.52 on the 1.5 mm candidate (study B: 0.57 on its cases; Rev K 0.56 on the same cases), words about
  6 → 9 of 10, tremor-free writing untouched.

**What changed or failed.**
- **Rev J's simulated power falls from 2.36 to 1.54 W** (about the 0.74 W the old power split had called the servo's
  reaction to sensor noise); the C1S nose's static load still dominates, so its hardware claims stay suspended. A
  2.22 Wh cell would last about 1.4 h.
- **Two small regressions in sim2j:** at mild tremor G4 is now slightly worse than the ordinary pen in 10 of 18 cases
  (7 of 18 before; 1.2 % on average) and in one case the recogniser lost a word on near-identical ink; and the held
  nose (the "ordinary pen" of every card) writes 9–27 µm worse, which is why G4's ratios look slightly better.
- **The mechanism limits got worse** where the servo slowed: perfect knowledge in sim2j 0.155 → 0.169 of the ordinary
  pen; on the balanced nib perfect knowledge leaves 0.33 of the held nib's error on Rev K instead of
  study B's 0.27 (the 40/46 Hz servo and the loads), and 0.54 at 12 Hz × 2 mm, where ±1.06 mm runs out; the 1.5 mm
  candidate keeps it at 0.24–0.27.
- **Rev J's gated tracker disturbs clean real writing more** with the causal page model: 41 µm on average (105 µm for
  the worst writer) instead of 25 µm, because its gate now opens on two of nine clean notes. A DeltaPen-class page
  position also becomes a worse tremor reference when used without refitting (1.3 mm left instead of 1.0–1.1 mm).
- **The balanced nib's power moves both ways.** In simulation it is lower than study B said (14.1 against 16.4 mW on
  study B's cases) because the 40/46 Hz servo draws 38 % less; but the 1.5 mm candidate costs 1.6 × Rev K's power
  (weaker force constant), and at the weaker axis, the disk minimum and the 0.7 derating its correcting power reaches
  about 190 mW (CALC on SIM). Its tremor-free writing alone costs about 29 mW at the weaker axis, above
  REQ-BNIB-004's 20 mW for duty A: an input to DEC-072's choice.
- **The rerun exposed six defects in the packages it imported** (§8), two of which change results silently: the
  "legacy" flags do not restore the old contact channel, so they do not reproduce G4's published rows; and the causal
  page model cannot run on any recorded note at all (every note starts with the pen lifted and version 2 raises). This
  study worked around each one in its own package and proposes a minimal patch for each owner.

**New numbers to quote** (all SIMULATION of proposed designs; synthetic inputs unless marked real):
- Rev J + G4 in sim2j: ink error 0.61 of the ordinary pen at 8–12 Hz × 1–2 mm (writer interval 0.60–0.63), words
  75 → 100 %, tremor-free writing 0 µm, 1.5 W; perfect knowledge 0.17; autowrite at 3 mm 68 % of words.
- Balanced nib in sim2 (DEC-066 servo, causal contact, corrected loads): G4 0.57 (Rev K) and 0.52 (the pass's 1.5 mm
  candidate) of the held nib, perfect knowledge 0.38 and 0.27, copper loss 20.5 and 32.1 mW at the x-axis centre while
  correcting 1–2 mm (84 and 194 mW in DEC-080's weakest × 0.7 convention, CALC on SIM). CANDN_SENTENCE
- Reach with B1's dynamics (HW1, real inputs, perfect knowledge, severe class): ±1.06 mm +1.6 words of 10 (fails
  DEC-055's +2), ±1.5 mm +3.2 (passes).
- Real inputs with page model version 2 (HW1): E's frozen design 0.69 × the ordinary pen's tip tremor, −0.2 words,
  DEC-055 still fails; Rev J's gated tracker moves clean writing 41 µm (was 25 µm); a DeltaPen-class page-position
  predictor leaves 1.3 mm (was 1.0–1.1 mm).

## 1. What changed, and what this study reran

The engineering pass of 30 September (commit `e09a15f`; the lead's review and DEC-070…074 followed) found that several
simulation results had been computed with models that gave the controller more information, or the mechanism less
load, than a real pen would have. DEC-070 suspends those results as device evidence until this study reruns them.

| Finding of the pass | Code now | What it touched | Rerun here |
|---|---|---|---|
| F1. sim2's nib servo used the exact simulator velocity and the true ball force as its contact gate | `velocity_source="hall"` (timestamped Hall differences, 300 Hz filter, no current on stale feedback), `contact_source="measured"` (the refill-slide channel, 1 kHz, 1 ms late) | sim2j (Rev J), study B (balanced nib in sim2), study K's servo check, study W | §3, §4 |
| F2. The 400 Hz inner loop is unstable with causal sensing | 80 Hz inner loop for Rev J (largest sampled pole 0.998) | sim2j | §3 |
| F3. The firmware's contact flag was immediate (the same 2 kHz tick) | sampled at 1 kHz and delivered 1 ms late; **no flag restores the old flag** (found here) | every sim2j controller that gates on contact (G4's detector) | §3 (mode `legacy_exact`) |
| F4. The page-sensor model (realdata/sensors.py v1) let a window's future endpoint set its error and restored motion lost in a dropout | version 2: causal, lost motion stays lost, absolute reference invalid until re-anchored; the moment fit's window definition also corrected | the DeltaPen-class ("\|deltapen") rows of studies R, E and F | §6 |
| F5–F7. Balanced-nib loads: harmonic spring and inertia summed in quadrature; Rev K's wires gain tension against the stiff 10,000 N/m anchor (18.2 mN at the stop, not 2 mN); the ball guide's 4 N preload gives about 8 mN of rolling drag, not 2.6 mN | `bnib/loads.py` fixed; wire and guide models in `revk/feasibility.py` | study B's and K's nib power and servo checks | §4 (loads applied in the simulation) |
| F8. DEC-066: Rev K's position loop 40 Hz, inner loop at most 46 Hz | – (study B ran 80 / 100 Hz) | study B's SIM numbers | §4, §5 |
| F9. The RL reward stopped charging tracking error when contact was lost | repaired; six new policies all rejected (DEC-073) | RL results | none in the register quotes a trained policy (§2) |
| F10. A result computed on the Rev J nose's servo and mass was quoted for the balanced nib | – | study F's reach check | §5 |
| F11. The accepted-word completion planner (ai3) ignored velocity, acceleration and jerk limits | replaced by the bounded planner; DEC-071 moves whole words out of the pen | ai3's completion claim (W-14) | superseded by the pass (§2) |
| F12. `readable/e11.py` picked its calibration notes by a seed stride that need not keep the writer | – | study E11's per-user gates (T-06) | not rerun (§9, EXP-X07) |

## 2. The impact register (task 1)

**What it is (a CALCULATION on the documents and code paths; no simulation).** Every row of the preserved upstream
register in `docs/claims_register.md` (the four tables "Tremor", "Writing help", "Hardware" and "Simulation"), plus the
headline statements of its preamble, with the model that produced the number and what the pass's findings do to it.
A row that mixes models is split into sub-rows (T-01a, T-01b, …), one model and one verdict each. The full register
is `results/rebaseline/impact_register.csv` (and `.json`, with the model and fault vocabularies); the table below lists
every SIM row. A test (`rebaseline/tests`) parses the register's four tables and checks that every row is covered and
that every row whose evidence says SIM has a verdict.

**Counts** (92 entries: 69 simulation entries plus 23 calculation, literature, data or manufacturer rows listed for
completeness; the ids follow the tables' order at commit `eb851a4`, and the test flags any row added later):

| Verdict | Entries | Which models |
|---|---|---|
| Affected, rerun here | **29** | sim2j with legacy sensing (11: the headline, perfect knowledge, the mild, slow and tremor-free cards, severe tremor, autowrite and its travel, Rev J's power ×3), HW1 with page model v1 (11), the balanced nib in sim2 (study B's and K's rows, 4), study F's reach on the Rev J plant (2), one no-page row whose comparison number is page-dependent (P-03) |
| Affected, not rerun (reason given per row) | **15** | sim2j legacy rows of devices or modes already dropped or not carried forward (heel wheel ×2, end-cap, gated listening ×2, TCN replay, guided tracing, lead-through, Rev J.1's temperature, the C1S nose's Km: 10), autowrite with the realistic page sensor (1, superseded in the pen by DEC-071), study W (2), E11's per-user gates (1), study B's thermal run (1) |
| Unaffected | 23 | H1 (3), HW1 with synthetic inputs (6), HW1-D (4), HW1 real inputs with no DeltaPen-class sensor (5), letters and language (3), the writer model (1), sim2's H1 verification (1) |
| Superseded by the pass | 2 | ai3's kinematic accepted-word completion (W-14); "RL for the nose: not trained" (S-03) |
| Not a simulation | 23 | CALC, LIT, DATA, MFR rows (listed, not judged; 6 of them added to the Hardware table on 30 September by studies H and N) |

**Model vocabulary.** `sim2j-legacy`: sim2 / MuJoCo whole Rev J pen with exact velocity, true-force gate, 400 Hz inner
loop and the immediate firmware contact flag. `sim2-bnib`: study B's `bnib/sim.py` set-up (an observer servo on the Hall
reading, so its velocity was already causal; the true contact as the servo's gate; linear wires; no guide drag).
`hw1-real-v1`: model HW1 with study R's recorded inputs and the page model version 1. `hw1-real-nopage`: the same
without any DeltaPen-class sensor (ordinary pen, perfect knowledge, the ideal bound). `hw1-real-revj-plant`: study F's
reach check (the Rev J nose's servo and mass). Others as named. Faults F1–F12 are listed in §1 and in the JSON.

**Reading the table.** "Rerun / reason" points to the results file (or gives the reason a row was not rerun);
"Outcome of the rerun" says what the rerun found for the published statement (SURVIVES, CHANGES, FAILS or UNCHANGED;
SIMULATION as labelled in §3–§6).

**RL.** No row of the preserved register quotes a trained RL policy: its only RL row says "not trained" (S-03), which
the pass superseded with six policies, none adopted (DEC-073). The reward fault (F9) therefore changes no register
number.

## 3. sim2j's headline cards under causal sensing (task 2)

**Set-up (SIMULATION: sim2 / MuJoCo with the whole Rev J pen and its C1S nose, PROPOSED DESIGN parameters; synthetic
v2 writers and synthetic essential tremor; nothing measured).** Exactly the historical cases, so every comparison is
paired: test writers 0–5 on their first test seed (writer *w*, seed 200 + (*w* mod 4)), "return library" after 4 s
on the paper, the H1 hand, a 50 µs step. The same controllers: the pen with the nose held centred by its own servo
(the "ordinary pen" column), the frozen guarded tracker G4 (`results/sim2j/rules.json`), and perfect knowledge of the
handle's tremor (the mechanism's limit). Each sensing mode re-learns the writer's adapted hand path on its own pen, as
the historical protocol does for each pen model. Three modes, one process each, all on the same current code:

| Mode | Nib velocity fed back | Servo's contact gate | Inner loop | Firmware's contact flag (G4's detector gate) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `causal` (the new default) | timestamped Hall differences, 300 Hz filter, zero current on stale feedback | delayed measured refill slide | 80 Hz | sampled at 1 kHz, delivered 1 ms late |
| `legacy_flags` | exact simulator velocity (`legacy_true`) | true ball force (`legacy_force`) | 400 Hz | sampled at 1 kHz, 1 ms late: **no flag restores the old flag** |
| `legacy_exact` (a reproduction check, writers 0–1) | as `legacy_flags` | as `legacy_flags` | 400 Hz | the historical flag (same 2 kHz tick, no delay), restored by a runtime substitution in this process |

**The headline survives causal sensing.** At 8–12 Hz × 1–2 mm (24 paired cases, SIMULATION as above):

| | Historical (sim2j/build rows, the published card) | Legacy flags, current code | **Causal sensing (the new default)** |
|---|---|---|---|
| Ink error with G4 ÷ ordinary pen (95 % bootstrap over cases; over writers) | 0.628 (0.60–0.66; 0.61–0.64) | 0.620 (0.59–0.65; 0.61–0.63) | **0.612 (0.58–0.64; 0.60–0.63)** |
| … at 1 mm / at 2 mm | 0.68 / 0.58 | 0.66 / 0.58 | **0.66 / 0.56** |
| Ink error left, mm (ordinary pen → G4): 1 mm / 2 mm | 0.41 → 0.28 / 0.93 → 0.54 | 0.41 → 0.27 / 0.93 → 0.54 | **0.43 → 0.28 / 0.94 → 0.53** |
| Words read, of 10 (ordinary → G4) | 7.7 → 10.0 | 7.7 → 10.0 | **7.5 → 10.0** |
| Letters read, of 10 | 7.9 → 9.4 | 7.9 → 9.4 | **8.0 → 9.4** |
| Tremor-free writing moved by G4 (6 writers) | 0 µm (max 0) | 0 µm | **0 µm (max 0)** |
| Perfect knowledge (mechanism limit) | 0.155 | 0.155 | **0.169** |
| Mean electrical power, ordinary → G4 (incl. 0.077 W electronics) | 2.36 → 2.36 W | 2.36 → 2.36 W | **1.54 → 1.52 W** |
| Tremor-free writing, power | 2.28 W | 2.28 W | **1.49 W** |

What moved, case by case (paired, 95 % intervals resampling the 6 writers; SIM):
- **G4's own ink is unchanged**: its absolute ink error changes by −1.1 µm (−17.5 to +10.4) against the historical
  rows. The ratio improves slightly (−0.016, −0.039 to −0.001) only because the reference got worse: with the causal
  80 Hz servo the held nose yields a little more, so the ordinary-pen column writes 14 µm worse (9 to 19 µm) and reads
  0.2 fewer words of 10. This is not a gain for the device.
- **The mechanism's limit is slightly worse**: perfect knowledge leaves 11 µm more ink error (7 to 16 µm); its ratio
  rises from 0.155 to 0.169 (most likely because the slower, causal inner loop follows the correction less
  closely; not isolated).
- **Power falls by a third** (2.36 → 1.54 W), about the 0.74 W that the old power split had called "mostly a model
  artefact" (the servo's reaction to its unfiltered sensor). The rest is still the static side
  load of the C1S nose (about 1.1 W, DEC-046), so Rev J's power and battery claims stay SUSPENDED: the 2.22 Wh cell
  lasts about 1.4 h at 1.5 W (CALC on SIM).
- **The feedback never went stale** after start-up: at most 2 servo ticks without valid feedback per run (the first
  two, before two Hall samples exist).
- **Legacy flags reproduce the old numbers for the pen without a tracker, not for G4.** The ordinary pen and perfect
  knowledge match the historical rows to within 0.03 µm (to 10⁻⁹ µm in 75 % and 58 % of the cases). G4 does not: its
  detector is gated by the firmware's contact flag, which the pass also delayed, with no switch. That alone moved G4's
  ratio by −0.008 on average (−0.019 to −0.000), by −0.14 and −0.04 in two cases, and left G4's ink identical (to
  10⁻⁹ µm) in only 4 of 24 cases. So `legacy_flags` separates the servo's sensing change (causal against legacy flags: −0.008,
  −0.020 to 0.000, not distinguishable from zero) from the firmware contact change (legacy flags against history:
  −0.008). With the historical flag restored at run time (`legacy_exact`, writers 0–1, 24 rows), every row reproduces
  the historical ink error to within 0.4 µm (0.1 %; identical to 10⁻⁹ µm in 11 of 24) and G4's ratio to within 0.0005,
  against 0.14 for `legacy_flags` on the same cases: the contact channel explains the whole difference (patch
  proposal 1).
- **The move is small by DEC-047's own yardstick**: 0.016, below the 0.05 that DEC-047 uses as its revisit line for
  new writers or seeds.

**The rest of the ET grid (the "mild" and "slow tremor" cards), causal sensing against the historical rows (SIM as
above, paired, 6 writers):**

| Card | Historical: ratio (writer interval); words ordinary → G4 | **Causal: ratio (writer interval); words ordinary → G4** | Perfect knowledge: historical → causal |
|---|---|---|---|
| Mild ET, 0.3 mm at 4, 8, 12 Hz (18 cases): "no gain, no harm" | 1.010 (0.99–1.04); 10.0 → 10.0 | **1.012 (0.99–1.04); 10.0 → 9.7** | 0.348 → 0.343 |
| Slow tremor, 4 Hz × 1–2 mm (12 cases): "the detector listens from 4.5 Hz" | 1.000 (1.000–1.001); 5.4 → 5.4 | **1.000 (1.000–1.001); 5.4 → 5.4** | 0.093 → 0.088 |
| Moderate ET, 1 mm at 8–12 Hz (12) | 0.679 (0.64–0.72); 10 → 10 | **0.661 (0.63–0.70); 10 → 10** | 0.158 → 0.170 |
| Strong ET, 2 mm at 8–12 Hz (12) | 0.576 (0.55–0.60); 5.4 → 10 | **0.563 (0.54–0.58); 5.0 → 10** | 0.152 → 0.167 |

- **Both claims survive** (T-11: mild 1.01; T-12: slow 1.00). Across all 54 paired ET cases G4's ratio moved by
  −0.006 (−0.014 to −0.000), again because the ordinary-pen column writes 9.5 µm worse (7.7 to 11.3 µm).
- **One regression to report**: at mild tremor G4 was worse than the ordinary pen in 10 of 18 cases (56 %) against 7
  of 18 historically (on average 1.2 % more ink error than the ordinary pen, as before), and in one case (writer 1,
  8 Hz × 0.3 mm) it lowered the words read from 10 to 5 of 10 although its ink error was 3 % lower than the ordinary
  pen's: the recogniser read "retarn" for "return" on G4's ink and "return" on the ordinary pen's (both read
  "librqry"). It is a recogniser threshold on near-identical ink (123 against 127 µm), not a correction that moved the
  letters, but it is exactly the kind of word a person would also have to re-read.
- **The mild-tremor regression comes from the causal servo, not from the contact channel**: with the legacy flags on
  the current code the mild card reads 1.005 (0.99–1.02), 10 → 10 words and 7 of 18 cases worse, as historically.
  Across all 54 ET cases the legacy flags reproduce the historical ordinary-pen and perfect-knowledge rows to 0.03 µm
  (identical to 10⁻⁹ µm in 78 % and 70 % of them); only G4's rows move (up to 60 µm in one case, through the contact
  channel, §3 above).

**Severe tremor and autowrite (the C1S nose's ±6 mm reach; SIM as above, causal sensing against the historical rows,
6 writers, 3 mm at 5 and 8 Hz):**

| Card | Historical | **Causal sensing** |
|---|---|---|
| Writing through severe tremor (12 cases): words of 10, ordinary → G4 | 0.4 → 3.8 | **0.4 → 4.2** |
| … ink error, mm, ordinary → G4 (ratio) | 1.47 → 1.15 (0.776) | **1.49 → 1.17 (0.773)** |
| … perfect knowledge (ratio; words) | 0.078; 10 | 0.086; 10 |
| … power, ordinary → G4 | 2.31 → 2.33 W | 1.47 → 1.49 W |
| Autowrite at 3 mm, the pen writes a known text (12 cases): words of 10 (ordinary pen 0.4) | 8.8 | **6.8** |
| … letters of 10; ink error to the planned letters | 8.5; 75 µm | **7.6; 101 µm** |
| … nose travel used, of 6.57 mm | 6.56 | 6.57 |
| Autowrite with no tremor (6 cases): words; ink error | 10; 45 µm | **10; 70 µm** |
| Autowrite power | 2.29 W | 1.47 W |

- **T-21 survives**: writing through 3 mm of synthetic tremor with G4 reads 4.2 instead of 3.8 words of 10 (the
  ratio moves by −0.003, −0.005 to −0.001), again with the held nose writing a little worse (27 µm, 22 to 33 µm).
- **Autowrite gets worse under causal sensing** (W-01b changes): at 3 mm it reads 6.8 instead of 8.8 words of 10,
  because the nose now follows its planned letters about 25 µm less accurately in every case (paired over all 36
  autowrite cases: +24.8 µm, 23.8 to 25.9; −0.8 words of 10, −1.2 to −0.3). Which part of the causal change costs it
  was not isolated (the legacy-flag autowrite run was dropped for time); the perfect-knowledge rows above show the
  same direction: the causal servo follows large, fast commands less closely. This is a mechanism result for the C1S
  bench module; in-pen autowrite is already superseded by DEC-071.
- **The travel statement survives** (T-22): at 3 mm the nose still uses its whole 6.57 mm.

## 4. The balanced nib in sim2 with DEC-066's servo and corrected loads (task 3)

**Set-up (SIMULATION: sim2 / MuJoCo through study B's `bnib/sim.py`, imported unchanged and configured at run time;
synthetic v2 writers and synthetic essential tremor; study B's DeltaPen-calibrated page sensor; sim2j's frozen tracker
G4; nib constants are CALCULATIONS for a PROPOSED DESIGN; nothing measured).** The synthetic-input half of EXP-E23.
The cells are study B's ET cells at 8 and 12 Hz × 1 and 2 mm (study B ran no 12 Hz × 2 mm cell; it is new here),
tremor-free writing, and three controllers: the nib held centred (the ordinary-pen column), G4, and perfect knowledge.
Writers 0–5 on their first test seed (study B used writers 0–3; the comparison with study B is on its writers and
cells). What changed, one step at a time (each a separate process; writers 0–1 for the intermediate steps):

| Configuration | Nib | Servo (position / inner) | Servo's contact gate and firmware contact | Suspension and guide |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `B1_studyB_exact` (reproduction check, writer 0) | study B's B1: Km 0.400 N/√W, 3.49 g, 3.79 N/m | 80 / 100 Hz | true contact; immediate flag (historical) | linear wires, no guide drag |
| `B1_studyB_now` | B1 | 80 / 100 Hz | **delayed measured contact** (current sim2j) | linear, no drag |
| `B1_dec066` | B1 | **40 / 46 Hz** (DEC-066) | delayed measured | linear, no drag |
| `revK_linear` | **Rev K's nib**: Km 0.3335 N/√W (x-axis centre), 3.44 g, 1.56 N/m | 40 / 46 Hz | delayed measured | linear, no drag |
| **`revK_corrected`** | Rev K, travel ±1.06 mm, stop 1.26 mm | 40 / 46 Hz | delayed measured | **nonlinear wire law with the stated 10,000 N/m anchor (11.5 mN at 1.06 mm, 18.2 mN at the stop) + 8.07 mN rolling drag of the ball guide** |
| **`cand15_corrected`** | the pass's 24 mm / 1.5 mm candidate: Km 0.2729 N/√W, 3.67 g, eight 0.10 × 34 mm wires on a 100 N/m anchor with 5 mN assembly tension (1.71 N/m tangent at the centre; 2.77 mN at 1.5 mm), stop 1.7 mm | 40 / 46 Hz | delayed measured | nonlinear wire law + 8.07 mN drag |
| `revK_linear_80` (for H-09) | Rev K, linear wires | 80 / 100 Hz | delayed measured | linear, no drag |
| `candN_corrected` (a first look, writers 0–1) | study N's balanced candidate (DEC-083): Km 0.398 N/√W, 3.29 g, eight 0.10 × 32.1 mm wires on a 50 N/m anchor, stop 1.7 mm | 40 / 46 Hz | delayed measured | nonlinear wire law + 3.83 mN drag (its 1.82 N preload) |

How the corrected loads enter: the wires' force beyond their linear stiffness (from `revk.feasibility.wire_anchor`,
the pass's beam-column with the anchor in series) and the guide's rolling drag (−8.07 mN·v/|v|·tanh(|v|/0.5 mm/s),
ASSUMPTION on the regularisation) are applied as generalised forces on the nib's two joints at every 50 µs physics
step. The explicit update is stable at this step (CALC: velocity multiplier 0.77 per step for Rev K near zero speed,
in (0, 1]; 0.78 for the candidate). The harmonic-load fix of `bnib/loads.py` (spring and inertia added coherently,
not in quadrature) needs no switch in a time-domain simulation: the simulated force is the physical sum. It matters for the CALC budgets, which
the pass has already recomputed (DEC-072). The servo's authority gate of `bnib/sim.py` still receives the TRUE contact
(its copy of the Rev J step predates the causal change); here it receives the firmware's delayed measured contact,
as `sim2j/stepper.py` now does (patch proposal 3). The sim2 nib is isotropic, so the simulation uses the x-axis force
constant at the centre on both axes; the weaker y-axis, the disk minimum and the 0.7 derating are CALC rescalings of
the simulated copper loss (P = F²/Km² at the same force demand). DEC-080 (study N, after this study's brief) makes
the weakest singular value over the usable disk × 0.7 the headline convention for every nib power claim, with the
centre value stated beside it: here that is the "disk minimum × 0.7" column. Like study B's, this simulation carries
no gravity load on the moving mass and no counter-face residual, which DEC-080's matched model adds (§9).

**Against study B as published, on study B's writers and cells** (SIMULATION as above; writers 0–3, ET 8 Hz × 1 and
2 mm and 12 Hz × 1 mm, 12 cases per controller; study B's figures are its own rows, `bnib/build/sim_rows.json`,
reproduced here to 0.0 µm):

| | Study B's B1 (80 / 100 Hz, linear wires, no drag, true-contact gate) | **Rev K, corrected (40 / 46 Hz, wire law, 8 mN drag, causal contact)** | **1.5 mm candidate, corrected** |
|---|---|---|---|
| Ink error with G4 ÷ held nib | 0.572 | **0.557** | **0.539** |
| … per cell (8 Hz 1 mm / 8 Hz 2 mm / 12 Hz 1 mm) | 0.655 / 0.594 / 0.466 | 0.598 / 0.586 / 0.488 | 0.595 / 0.558 / 0.464 |
| Perfect knowledge ÷ held nib (the mechanism's limit) | 0.268 | **0.329** | **0.237** |
| Words of 10: held → G4 | 7.1 → 9.6 | 7.1 → 9.2 | 7.1 → 9.2 |
| Tremor-free writing moved by G4 | 0 µm | **0 µm** | **0 µm** |
| Nib copper loss with G4 / tremor-free writing (x-axis Km) | 16.4 / 11.8 mW | **14.1 / 9.5 mW** | **22.2 / 15.0 mW** |
| Hours per charge with G4 / tremor-free (CALC on SIM, the pen's cell and electronics) | 32.6 / 35.3 h | 34.0 / 36.9 h | 29.7 / 33.4 h |

**All six writers and all four cells** (24 cases per controller; the 12 Hz × 2 mm cell is new):

| | Rev K, corrected | 1.5 mm candidate, corrected |
|---|---|---|
| Ink error with G4 ÷ held nib (95 % writer interval) | **0.566 (0.552–0.581)** | **0.521 (0.507–0.534)** |
| … at 12 Hz × 2 mm | 0.568 | 0.443 |
| Perfect knowledge ÷ held nib (… at 12 Hz × 2 mm) | 0.379 (0.537) | 0.273 (0.391) |
| Words of 10: held → G4 (perfect knowledge) | 5.8 → 9.2 (8.8) | 6.0 → 9.2 (9.4) |
| Letters of 10: held → G4 | 6.9 → 8.8 | 7.0 → 9.2 |
| Tremor-free writing moved by G4, mean (max) | 0 (0) µm | 0 (0) µm |
| Nib copper loss with G4 / held / tremor-free, x-axis Km (SIM) | 20.5 / 24.4 / 11.7 mW | 32.1 / 39.4 / 18.3 mW |
| … with G4 at the weaker axis / the disk minimum / the disk minimum × 0.7 derating (CALC on SIM) | 30.8 / 41.2 / 84.1 mW | 50.0 / 95.2 / 194.3 mW |

**Answer.** The balanced nib's synthetic benefit **survives** causal sensing, DEC-066's servo and the corrected loads:
G4 removes about 43 % (Rev K) and 48 % (the candidate) of the ink error of a held nib at 8–12 Hz × 1–2 mm, lifts
words from about 6 to 9 of 10, and never moves tremor-free writing. Against study B on its own cases the G4 ratio is
even slightly lower (0.557 against 0.572), but that is not a gain: one case of study B was hurt by the old contact
channel (the ladder below), and the held nib, the comparison, now yields more. **What gets worse is the mechanism's limit**
on Rev K: perfect knowledge leaves 0.33 of the held nib's error instead of 0.27 (the slower servo and the loads),
and 0.54 at 12 Hz × 2 mm, where ±1.06 mm saturates. The candidate's ±1.5 mm keeps the limit at 0.24–0.27.
**Power:** in simulation the nib draws less than study B said (14.1 against 16.4 mW on study B's cases): DEC-066's
slower servo draws 38 % less (the ladder below), more than Rev K's weaker force constant (+43 %) and the loads add.
In DEC-080's convention (weakest point × 0.7) the same force demand costs 84 mW (Rev K) and 194 mW (the candidate)
with 1–2 mm tremor, and 48 and 111 mW in tremor-free writing (CALC on SIM) — the same range as the pass's duty screen for the candidate (81 mW at 20 mN, 189 mW
at 40 mN). **A flag for DEC-072:** the candidate's tremor-free writing alone costs 18 mW at the x-axis centre and
about 29 mW at its weaker axis (CALC on SIM, 50° tilt), above REQ-BNIB-004's 20 mW for duty A (0.2 mm rms tremor, mean
over 35–75°); Rev K's costs 12 and 18 mW. These are simulated force demands of a proposed design, not measurements.

**What each correction did, one at a time** (SIMULATION as above; writers 0–1, study B's three cells ET 8 Hz × 1 and
2 mm and 12 Hz × 1 mm, 6 cases per controller; the fourth cell, 12 Hz × 2 mm, in brackets where it matters):

| Step | Ratio G4 / perfect knowledge | Ink error, held → G4, µm | Words of 10, held → G4 | Nib power with G4 / held nib / tremor-free writing, mW |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Study B's own rows (`bnib/build/sim_rows.json`) | 0.578 / 0.271 | 715 → 415 | 7.5 → 9.2 | 15.8 / 15.9 / 11.2 |
| `B1_studyB_exact` on the current code (writer 0) | reproduces study B's 9 rows to **0.0 µm** | | | |
| + causal contact channel (`B1_studyB_now`) | **0.540** / 0.271 | 715 → 396 | 7.5 → 9.2 | 15.8 / 15.9 / 11.2 |
| + DEC-066's 40 / 46 Hz servo (`B1_dec066`) | 0.535 / **0.308** | **780 → 429** | 7.5 → **8.3** | **9.8 / 11.3 / 5.7** |
| + Rev K's nib constants, linear wires (`revK_linear`) | 0.535 / 0.309 | 781 → 429 | 7.5 → 8.3 | **14.0 / 16.4 / 8.1** |
| + corrected loads: wire law and 8 mN guide drag (`revK_corrected`) | **0.553 / 0.340** | 774 → 435 | 7.5 → 9.2 | 13.5 / 15.5 / **8.9** |
| The 1.5 mm candidate with the same corrections (`cand15_corrected`) | 0.532 / **0.249** | 774 → 415 | 7.5 → 9.2 | **21.4 / 24.8 / 14.1** |

- **The causal contact channel changed one case.** None of the held-nib or perfect-knowledge rows moved (≤ 0.1 µm)
  and the power did not change; G4 moved in one case of six — writer 0 at 8 Hz × 1 mm, 0.83 → 0.60 — in G4's favour.
  It is the same case that moved in sim2j (§3, 0.86 → 0.72): the old immediate contact flag disturbed G4's detector
  there. So study B's published G4 figure for this cell (0.655) was pessimistic by this one case.
- **DEC-066's slower servo costs mechanism, saves power.** The held nib yields more (its ink error rises 9 %, 715 →
  780 µm), G4's absolute ink rises 8 % while its ratio is unchanged, perfect knowledge worsens from 0.271 to 0.308, and
  one case reads fewer words with G4. The nib's copper loss falls by 38 % with G4 and by half in tremor-free writing.
  This is study K's servo check (H-09: "at 40/46 Hz the ink error rose 7 % and power fell 29 %") with causal sensing:
  with Rev K's constants run at both rates (`revK_linear_80` against `revK_linear`), 40/46 Hz raises G4's ink error
  8 % (396 → 429 µm; 12 % with the 12 Hz × 2 mm cell), the held nib's 9 %, and cuts the copper loss 38 % with G4 and
  49 % in tremor-free writing (22.4 → 14.0 and 15.9 → 8.1 mW); perfect knowledge goes from 0.271 to 0.309, and G4's
  words fall from 10 to 8.3 of 10 in these six cases (the two-word text quantises words coarsely). Study K found +7 %
  and −29 % on two tuning writers: **the claim survives in direction, with a larger power saving**.
- **Rev K's nib constants change only the power**: the ink is the same to 2 µm; the copper loss rises by (0.400 /
  0.3335)² = 1.44 × at the same force (CALC; SIM 1.43 ×).
- **The corrected loads cost a little mechanism and almost no power.** The wires' hardening and the guide's drag
  (8.0–8.6 mN rms on the carrier while correcting, the drag dominating) raise G4's ratio by 0.018 (+0.067 in the worst
  case, 12 Hz × 1 mm) and perfect knowledge's by 0.031, and add 0.8 mW in tremor-free writing; while correcting, the
  copper loss is even 0.5 mW lower (probably because the drag damps the carrier's motion; not isolated). The drag
  step is stable (CALC above).
- **The 1.5 mm candidate buys reach with power.** Its perfect-knowledge ratio is the best of all (0.249; 0.291 with
  the 2 mm cell, where Rev K's ±1.06 mm saturates: 0.395), and G4 does as well as on Rev K; its copper loss is 1.6 ×
  Rev K's in every row, consistent with its weaker x-axis force constant ((0.334 / 0.273)² = 1.49, CALC) and its
  7 % heavier carrier.

**A first look at study N's balanced candidate** (DEC-083 adopted it for the coupon and the CAD after this study's
brief; SIMULATION as above, writers 0–1, the four ET cells; its constants from `results/nibopt/candidates.json`:

## 5. Study F's reach check with the balanced nib's dynamics (task 4)

**Set-up (SIMULATION: model HW1 of `handwriting/` with study R's REAL recorded inputs — UNIPEN hpb2 writing, UCI PD
tip tremor, Zenodo ET hand tremor — on the TUNING split only, 20 cases: 10 notes of 5 writers × PD and ET at the
severe class, 1.72 mm at the tip; perfect knowledge of the tremor; nothing measured).** Study F cut the Rev J nose's
travel to ±1.0 and ±1.5 mm but kept Rev J's servo (80 Hz follower, 400 Hz idealised inner loop) and its 2.10 g
tip-equivalent mass. Here the same cases run with the balanced nib's servo (DEC-066: 40 Hz position loop, 46 Hz inner
loop) and its moving mass, linear wire stiffness and force limit: Rev K's nib (3.44 g, 1.56 N/m, Km 0.3335 N/√W at the
x-axis centre) at ±1.0, ±1.06 and ±1.5 mm, and the 24 mm / 1.5 mm candidate (3.67 g, 1.53 N/m, Km 0.273 N/√W) at
±1.5 mm. Every pen learns its own adapted hand path and its own nose-held run; perfect knowledge previews its own servo
group delay (6.2 ms for B1, 3.4 ms for Rev J). Words are read by study R's literal AI reader for the two design points
(B1 Rev K at ±1.06 mm, the candidate at ±1.5 mm) and, for every run, through the frozen E13 tuning curve (CALC). The
ordinary pen's words of the same cases are study F's reading (0.76 of 10). DEC-055's line (+2 words of 10 over the
ordinary pen at the severe class, 95 % writer-bootstrap interval above 0) is applied to perfect knowledge, i.e. as a
**necessary condition on the mechanism, not a tracker result**.

**Reproduction.** Study F's own Rev J runs at ±1.0 and ±1.5 mm were recomputed on the same code and agree to 0.0 mm
(all 40 cases).

| Pen (servo; moving mass) | Travel | Tip tremor left, mm (95 % writer interval) | Time at the travel limit | Words read of 10 | Gain over the ordinary pen, read | DEC-055 words line | Gain via the frozen curve (CALC) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Rev J (study F's pen, reproduced) | ±1.0 mm | 1.00 (0.94–1.06) | 64 % | 2.2 (study F) | +1.4 (study F) | fails | +0.7 (0.3–1.1) |
| Rev J (study F's pen, reproduced) | ±1.5 mm | 0.67 (0.60–0.74) | 40 % | 4.0 (study F) | +3.2 (study F) | passes | +2.0 (1.4–2.8) |
| **B1, Rev K's nib (40/46 Hz; 3.44 g)** | ±1.0 mm | 1.02 (0.95–1.08) | 64 % | – | – | – | +0.6 (0.2–1.1) |
| **B1, Rev K's nib** | **±1.06 mm** | **0.97 (0.90–1.04)** | 61 % | **2.4** | **+1.6 (0.7 to 2.4)** | **fails** (mean below +2) | +0.7 (0.3–1.2) |
| B1, Rev K's nib | ±1.5 mm | 0.69 (0.61–0.76) | 40 % | – | – | – | +2.0 (1.3–2.7) |
| **B1, the 1.5 mm candidate (40/46 Hz; 3.67 g)** | **±1.5 mm** | **0.69 (0.61–0.76)** | 40 % | **4.0** | **+3.2 (2.6 to 3.8)** | **passes** | +2.0 (1.3–2.7) |

(SIMULATION, HW1 + real inputs, tuning split, perfect knowledge; 20 cases, 5 writers; intervals resample writers.)

**Answer: yes — with the balanced nib's own servo and mass, ±1.5 mm still clears DEC-055's +2 words at the severe
class, as a mechanism bound, and ±1.06 mm still does not.**
- **The B1 dynamics cost almost nothing under perfect knowledge**: 0.017 mm more tremor left at ±1.5 mm (0.691
  against 0.674 mm) and 0.016 mm at ±1.0 mm. The 40 Hz servo's longer group delay is previewed exactly by perfect
  knowledge, and the moving mass (3.44 or 3.67 g against 2.10 g) and the force constant do not separate the two nibs
  at ±1.5 mm (0.6906 and 0.6909 mm). **A real tracker cannot preview the delay**: this result bounds the mechanism
  only (study F: the best causal estimator leaves about 1.1 mm).
- **Words read**: the candidate at ±1.5 mm reads 4.0 of 10 (+3.2, 2.6–3.8), the same as study F's +3.2 for Rev J at
  ±1.5 mm. Rev K's ±1.06 mm reads 2.4 (+1.6, 0.7–2.4): its interval stays above 0 but its mean is below +2, so it fails
  the line, as study F's ±1.0 mm did (+1.4).
- **By tremor type** (case means, SIM): at ±1.5 mm the PD cases gain +2.1 words (0.1 → 2.2) and the ET cases +4.4
  (1.4 → 5.8); at ±1.06 mm PD gains +1.0 and ET +2.2. The PD half of the severe class is the binding one: at ±1.5 mm
  it sits at the line.
- **The literal reader and the frozen curve disagree by about 1.3 words** at ±1.5 mm (+3.2 read, +2.0 via the curve,
  whose lower bound 1.3 is below the line). Study F saw the same gap. The curve was fitted on the tuning split and is
  the more conservative of the two; both keep ±1.06 mm below the line.
- **The command exceeds 1 mm 61 % and 1.5 mm 37 % of the contact time for every pen** (as in study F: the severe
  class asks for more than any of these nibs has); at ±1.5 mm the nib sits at its travel limit 40 % of the time.

What this changes: study F's reach conclusion (P-04, T-08: "±1.0 mm gains 1.4 words; about ±1.5 mm needed") survives
the correction of its plant; the numbers move by at most 0.02 mm and 0.2 words. It remains a statement about perfect
knowledge.

## 6. The page-sensor rows of studies R, E and F with page model version 2 (task 5)

**Set-up (SIMULATION: model HW1 with study R's REAL recorded inputs; the DeltaPen-class page model of
`realdata/sensors.py` version 2 — an ASSUMPTION informed by LIT OPT-02 — installed in memory for these processes only;
a re-analysis of test cases studies R, E and F have already inspected, not a new test).** Version 2 draws each 10 ms
window's error from the preceding window only (independent seeded streams, so a longer record never changes an earlier
reading), keeps motion lost in a dropout lost, and marks the absolute reference invalid after a loss. Its amplitude is
fitted by the same moment match on the same tuning notes: c = 19.38 µm, σ = 1.353 (version 1 as published: 20.48 µm,
1.354; the pass also corrected the fit's window count, which moves c by −5.4 %, CALC). Every recorded note starts with
the pen lifted, which version 2 as written cannot handle (patch proposal 6); every case here is anchored at its first
valid page report (sample 262–263 of each record) by the runtime wrapper `rebaseline.page_v2.anchored`.

- **R:** study R's test cases (9 notes × PD/ET × severe/moderate/mild = 54, the 9 clean notes, and the 8 real-real
  bridge cases at 1 mm), with R's three trackers on the DeltaPen-class sensor (`revH_akf|deltapen`,
  `revJ_gated|deltapen`, `revJ_tcn|deltapen`) rerun with R's case keys, seeds and reading budget. The ordinary pen,
  perfect knowledge and the ideal-sensor rows use no DeltaPen-class sensor and are R's cached rows.
- **E:** study E's frozen designs on the same streams: `revJ_new|deltapen` (the frozen design), `revJ_g4|deltapen` (G4
  in HW1) and the four information rows, E's reading budget; DEC-055's line recomputed with E's rule.
- **F:** every configuration of study F's gap decomposition (20 tuning and 18 test severe cases) and its page sensing
  check (the tremor alone, tuning split, cross-fitted).

Every rerun case was checked to be the same case as the published one (writer, tremor record and amplitude): 71 of 71
matched. The version-2 window error on these streams averaged 37.1 µm (median per 10 ms window; mean 85.5 µm) against
34.4 µm for version 1 (LIT OPT-02, the DeltaPen measurement it imitates: 23.6 µm median, 68.3 µm mean); the
absolute reference stayed valid for 1.8 % of each record on average (it is lost at the first lift, as version 2
intends; none of R's, E's or F's trackers uses it).

**Studies R and E at the severe class (SIMULATION, HW1 + real inputs, 18 cases of 9 test writers, PD and ET pooled;
words of 10 read by study R's literal AI reader; tip tremor in mm peak and as a ratio to the ordinary pen; 95 %
intervals resample writers):**

What this means (SIM; the test split is spent, so these are re-analyses, not new tests):
- **Every severe-class conclusion of studies R and E survives.** No tracker helps on real severe tremor with either
  page model: words read stay at 0.1–0.4 of 10 against the ordinary pen's 0.5 and perfect knowledge's 7.0, and the
  tip-tremor ratios of R's trackers and E's designs move by at most 0.007 in the mean (single cases move by up to
  0.21 mm: Rev J's gated tracker on writer 7's PD case, 1.55 → 1.34 mm, better with version 2). At the moderate and
  mild classes their means move by at most 0.003 mm (Rev J's gated tracker reads 5.7 instead of 5.5 words at the
  moderate class). E's GLG information gate moves more (moderate 1.09 → 1.13, mild 1.13 → 1.21 of the ordinary pen):
  consistent with its gate opening more often on version 2's noise (not isolated here).
- **DEC-055's line still fails, with more margin**: E's frozen design gains −0.22 words (−0.44 to 0.00; v1 −0.05)
  and moves clean writing 68.9 µm on average and 504 µm for the worst writer (limits 25 and 50 µm); G4 gains −0.17
  and passes the clean-writing part (0.3 µm). The words difference (0.49 → 0.32 of 10) is the reader's threshold on
  near-identical tip tremor (1.117 → 1.118 mm), not a change in the tracker.
- **One regression to report: Rev J's gated tracker now disturbs clean real writing more** — 41.0 µm on average
  (worst writer 105 µm) instead of 25.5 µm (85 µm) — because its gate opened on two of the nine clean notes (7.5 % and
  2.6 % of the time) where it never opened with version 1. The same tracker with an ideal page sensor moves clean
  writing 25.1 µm. The GLG information gate shows the same effect (28.6 → 44.1 µm; worst 125 → 249 µm). So the claim
  "on real writing the Rev H and Rev J gated trackers moved it 25 µm (gate shut 99.8 %)" (T-13b) holds for Rev H but
  **changes** for Rev J's gated tracker, and study R's statement that the page sensor changes results by at most 0.1
  word and 0.01 mm (H-20) holds for words and tip tremor (v2: 0.0 words, 0.006 mm) but **not for clean writing**
  (+15.9 µm for Rev J's gated tracker).
- **E's network row does not move at all** (0.972 mm, 2.5 µm; identical to the last digit): it reads the IMU and the
  contact channel only (`realtrack/netmodel.features`). Its "|deltapen" label is a naming convention, not a
  dependence (T-04 is unaffected).
- **The bridge cases** (real handwriting, real tremor at 1 mm) move by at most 0.004 mm.

**Study F's gap decomposition (SIMULATION, HW1 + real inputs; 20 tuning and 18 test severe cases; tip tremor in mm,
writer means; words via the frozen E13 curve are CALC).** Every configuration of `readable.gap.run_case` was recomputed
with version 2 installed. The configurations that do not read the page position (perfect knowledge, prediction on the
true tremor, the IMU filters, the ideal-page rows, the held nib, and the real-data network, which reads only the IMU and
the contact channel) came out **identical to study F's published values to the last digit** (largest change 0.000 mm,
both splits): a built-in check that nothing else moved.

| Configuration (DeltaPen-class page streams) | Tuning: v1 → v2, mm | Test: v1 → v2, mm | Words via curve, test: v1 → v2 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Study E's chosen TCN, with writing, gated (`ai2tcn_full_gated`) | 1.116 → 1.116 | 1.117 → 1.118 | 1.13 → 1.12 |
| … tremor alone, gated (`ai2tcn_trem_gated`) | 1.031 → 1.028 | 1.053 → 1.055 | 1.25 → 1.24 |
| Ungated AKF, with writing (`akf_full_raw`) | 0.919 → 0.920 | 0.952 → 0.945 | 1.49 → 1.50 |
| … tremor alone (`akf_trem_raw`) | 0.733 → 0.732 | 0.750 → 0.739 | 2.21 → 2.27 |
| **Linear predictor on the page position, tremor alone (`page_ar_trem_deltapen`)** | **1.136 → 1.311** | **1.033 → 1.285** | **1.29 → 0.88** |
| (for scale) held nib / ideal page sensor, same predictor | 1.847 / 0.105 | 1.767 / 0.120 | 0.52 / 8.06 |

- **The estimators' gap is unchanged**: with writing present E's designs still leave 0.92–1.20 mm (the largest change
  of any estimator row is 0.012 mm), so study F's conclusion (separation, not prediction or
  sensing, is what is missing; about 1.1 mm left) survives.
- **The page sensor as a tremor reference gets worse**: predicting the tremor from the DeltaPen-class page position
  leaves 1.29–1.31 mm with version 2 instead of 1.03–1.14 mm (+0.17 to +0.25 mm), against 0.10–0.12 mm with an ideal
  page sensor. The likely cause (not isolated here) is that version 2 keeps the motion lost in outliers and dropouts
  lost, so the position steps at every loss and the high-passed predictor passes the steps into the tremor band;
  version 1 restored that motion from the truth. This strengthens, not weakens, F's finding that the DeltaPen-class
  sensor cannot serve as the tremor reference.
- **Every recorded case starts with the pen lifted** (first valid page sample 262–263 of each record), so version 2
  as written raises on all 38 cases; they were run with the anchored wrapper of patch proposal 6. After anchoring, the
  absolute page reference stays valid for only 1.8 % of each record on average (6.5 % at most): version 2 loses it at
  the first lift, as intended. None of R's, E's or F's trackers use the absolute reference, so this does not move their
  numbers, but any planner that needs it (DEC-074's bound execution, ai3's reachable-word check) will refuse almost
  always with this sensor class unless it is re-anchored.

**Study F's page sensing check** (the tremor alone on the tuning split; a linear predictor on the high-passed page
position, refitted per fold on the sensor's own streams; SIM streams, tip = SIM): with the DeltaPen-class sensor it
leaves 0.588 mm at the tip with version 1 and **0.564 mm** with version 2 (signal residual 0.591 → 0.566 mm); the
ideal-sensor row is unchanged (0.340 mm), as it must be. So when the predictor is refitted to version 2's streams the
page sensor supports about the same 0.56–0.59 mm as before; the gap rows above apply F's predictor fitted on the true
tremor, without refitting it to the sensor, and those get worse. Either way the DeltaPen-class page position alone stays above the 0.55 mm target of
DEC-067 with the writing removed, and far above it with the writing present.

## 7. Which headline claims survive

"Survives" means the rerun with the corrected model supports the published statement within its stated precision;
"changes" means the statement holds in direction but a quoted number moves beyond it; "fails" means the statement no
longer holds. Every row is SIMULATION (or CALC where marked); none is evidence of benefit to people.

| Claim (register id) | Published | Rerun (this study, model and sensing as in §3–§6) | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| **HEADLINE** Rev J + G4, ET 1–2 mm at 8–12 Hz (T-02a) | 0.63 (0.59–0.66); words 77 → 100 % | 0.61 (0.58–0.64); words 75 → 100 %; G4's own ink unchanged (sim2j, causal sensing, synthetic) | **Survives** (synthetic only) |
| Rev J + G4 moves tremor-free writing 0 mm (T-13a) | 0 µm | 0 µm (max 0) | **Survives** |
| Mild tremor 1.01, slow tremor 1.00 (T-11, T-12) | 1.01; 1.00 | 1.01; 1.00 (one mild case lost a word to the recogniser) | **Survives** |
| Writing through severe 3 mm tremor: words 4 → 38 % (T-21) | 4 → 38 %; 1.47 → 1.15 mm | 4 → 42 %; 1.49 → 1.17 mm | **Survives** |
| Autowrite: 88 % of words at 3 mm, 100 % with no tremor (W-01b); travel runs out at 3 mm (T-22) | 88 %; 100 %; 6.55 of 6.57 mm | 68 %; 100 %; 6.57 of 6.57 mm; ink +25 µm per case | **Changes** (worse) for words; travel **survives** |
| Perfect knowledge, Rev J: 0.10–0.20 at 8–12 Hz (T-01b) | 0.10–0.20; pool 0.155 | 0.11–0.22; pool 0.169 | **Changes** (slightly worse) |

## 8. Patch proposals for other packages (not applied: those folders are read-only for this study)

Each is a minimal change for the package's owner; this study worked around each one inside `rebaseline/` (runtime
substitution in its own process) and names the workaround.

1. **`sim2j/sensing.py`: the legacy flags do not restore the historical firmware contact channel.** The engineering
   pass changed the firmware's contact flag from "slide reading of the same 2 kHz tick" to "sampled at 1 kHz and
   delivered 1 ms late", with no switch. With `legacy_true` / `legacy_force` / 400 Hz the ordinary pen and perfect
   knowledge reproduce the historical rows to 0.03 µm, but G4 does not (its detector is gated by that flag): in two of
   the 24 headline cases the ratio moved by 0.04–0.14 (and by 0.23 in one case of study B's set-up, which shares the
   channel). Proposed: an explicit `Sensors.firmware_contact =
   "delayed" | "legacy_immediate"` (default "delayed"), read in `OnlineSensors.read`:
   `if self.pm.cfg.sensors.firmware_contact == "legacy_immediate": out["contact"] = bool(s_now > stop + 0.1e-3)` with
   `s_now = d.qpos[self.js] + nz[8] * self.slide_noise` every tick. Workaround here:
   `rebaseline.sim2j_cards._historical_contact_read` (mode `legacy_exact`), which reproduces the historical rows to
   0.4 µm (G4's ratio to 0.0005), and study B's rows to 0.0 µm (`bnib_rerun`, configuration `B1_studyB_exact`).
2. **`sim2j/et.py`: the writer-setup cache key ignores the nib's sensing mode.** `WriterSetup._cache_path` includes the
   nose's parameters only when Km or the flexure are unusual, so a causal run in a clone that already holds
   `sim2j/build/setups/` silently reuses a hand path the writer learned on the legacy pen (for writer 0 the two paths
   differ by up to 265 µm). Proposed: append `velocity_source`, `contact_source` and `inner_hz` of `pm.cfg.nose` to
   the key string. Workaround here: one setup folder per sensing mode under `rebaseline/build/sim2j/`.
3. **`bnib/sim.py` and `wholepen/stepper.py`: their copies of the Rev J step still pass the TRUE contact to the
   servo.** `sim2j/stepper.py` now passes the delayed measured contact unless `contact_source` is `legacy_force`; the
   two copies were not updated (`BStepper.step`, `servo.ref_tick(..., in_c, ...)`; wholepen likewise). Proposed: the
   same one-line gate as `RevJStepper.step`. Workaround here: `rebaseline.bnib_rerun` wraps the servo's `ref_tick` so
   that it receives the firmware's delayed contact (configurations marked `contact: current`).
4. **`realdata/hw1.py`: `page_model()` overwrites the version-1 fit.** On first use after the pass it refits and saves
   version 2 over `realdata/build/cache/page_model.json`, the file the historical studies used (in this clone the file
   was rewritten at 12:32 on 30 September). The refit is not the same fit: the pass also corrected the window
   definition of the moment fit (a 10 ms window now spans 10 sample intervals, not 9), so `c` fell from 20.48 µm to
   19.38 µm (−5.4 %) with `sigma` 1.354 → 1.353 (CALC). The version-1 record is lost from the cache. Proposed: save
   version 2 as `page_model_v2.json` and keep the version-1 file. Workaround here: the version-2 model is fitted in
   memory and never saved; the version-1 fit is recorded in `rebaseline/page_v2.py` (`V1_PUBLISHED_FIT`) from this
   study's first read of the file.
5. **`realdata/hw1.py`, `realtrack/test.py`, `readable/`: case caches do not record the page-model version.** A partial
   rerun on current code would reuse version-1 case files and add version-2 ones, then aggregate them together.
   Proposed: store `page_model_version` in every case JSON and refuse to aggregate mixed versions. Workaround here:
   all version-2 cases are written to `rebaseline/build/page_v2/`, and every card compares the full version-1 set with
   the full version-2 set.
6. **`realdata/sensors.py`: version 2 cannot run on the recorded notes at all.** `degrade_page` (version 2) raises
   "Initial optical position needs a valid anchor" when the first page sample is invalid, and every recorded note of
   studies R, E and F starts with the pen lifted (note 0 of the tuning split: first valid sample 262 of 32,996). So on
   current code none of the DeltaPen-class rows of R, E or F can be recomputed: they fail rather than change. Proposed
   (in `degrade_page`, version 2 only): anchor at the first valid report instead of raising, i.e. run the model from
   the first valid index `k`, report the samples before `k` as invalid with their availability monotone, and mark the
   absolute reference invalid before `k`; raise only when no sample is valid. Workaround here:
   `rebaseline.page_v2.anchored`, which does exactly that around the unchanged function (a test checks that from the
   anchor on the output equals version 2 on the suffix, that a record starting valid is untouched, and that version 1
   passes through).

## 9. Limitations, and what was not rerun

- **Every result is a simulation of a proposed design.** sim2 ranks concepts (COU-1) until EXP-V01/V02/V04 calibrate it
  and EXP-V05 validates it; HW1 is a simpler 2-D model. The causal sensing models (the Hall velocity's delay and noise,
  the contact channel's rate and latency, the page model version 2) are themselves ASSUMPTIONS until the bench measures
  them (EXP-T09, EXP-T10, EXP-T04). "Causal" means that no future or hidden information reaches the controller, not
  that the numbers are right.
- **Synthetic inputs in sim2.** Tasks 2 and 3 use the synthetic v2 writers and synthetic tremor, one seed per writer
  (the historical protocol); six writers are a small sample, and the intervals describe these cases, not a
  population. A second seed per writer was not run (EXP-X01).
- **The recogniser is a threshold.** Words and letters are read by the app's recogniser (sim2) or study R's literal AI
  reader (HW1); a few µm of ink can flip a word (§3's mild case, §6's clean notes). Differences of a word or less in
  one case are not signals; the pooled numbers and their writer intervals are.
- **Real inputs, spent split.** Task 5 re-analyses test cases that studies R, E and F have already inspected; it cannot
  confirm a design choice (EXP-X08 asks for a fresh split). Task 4 uses the tuning split only, as study F did.
- **Perfect knowledge is a mechanism bound, not a tracker.** Task 4's words gained assume the nib knows the tremor
  exactly and previews its own servo delay; any real estimator does worse (study F: about 1.1 mm left today).
- **The nib's force constant is isotropic in sim2.** Task 3 simulates the x-axis centre value; the weaker y-axis, the
  disk minimum and the 0.7 field derating are CALC rescalings of the simulated copper loss (EXP-X05).
- **HW1 cannot carry the nib's nonlinear loads.** Task 4 changes the servo bandwidth, the moving mass, the linear wire
  stiffness and the force limit; the wires' hardening and the guide's rolling drag enter only in task 3 (EXP-X06).
- **The guide drag and the wire anchor are the pass's CALC values** (8.07 mN at 4 N preload with an ASSUMED rolling
  coefficient; the stated 10,000 N/m and 100 N/m anchors); EXP-J17 and EXP-K20 measure them (EXP-X02 reruns task 3
  with the measured values).
- **Not rerun (reasons per row in the register):** sim2j's heel-wheel, end-cap, gated-listening and TCN-replay
  columns (devices or trackers already dropped); guided tracing, write-big loops and lead-through (wheel-driven or not
  carried forward: EXP-X04); study W's tails and collar (not adopted, DEC-051); study E11's per-user gates
  (information only; two faults touch them: EXP-X07); study B's thermal run (its coil rise scales with the
  re-simulated power); Rev J.1's temperature and the C1S nose's Km sensitivity (the C1S nose is not carried forward);
  autowrite with the realistic page sensor (W-02: superseded in the pen by DEC-071; EXP-X03).
  Dropped for time: the second test seed per writer (EXP-X01) and the legacy-flag runs of the severe and autowrite
  blocks (so the cause of autowrite's loss is not split between the servo and the contact channel); study N's
  balanced candidate ran on writers 0–1 only.
- **The simulated nib carries no gravity load** (`bnib/sim.py` runs with gravity off, as study B did), and no
  counter-face residual: DEC-080's matched model adds both (about 29.5 mN of weight across the pen at 35° and
  11–13 mN of residual, study H). A steady side force F adds F²/Km² to the copper loss: for 29.5 mN about 8 mW at
  Rev K's x-axis centre and 32 mW at its derated disk minimum (CALC). The SIM powers here compare with study B's,
  not with DEC-080's matched budgets.

## 10. Files, commands, compute and tests

**Package `rebaseline/`** (imports sim2, sim2j, bnib, realdata, realtrack, readable, revk, handwriting read-only; every
change of their behaviour is a runtime substitution inside this package's own processes, named in the results):

| File | What it does |
|---|---|
| `rebaseline/__init__.py` | paths; one numerical thread; numba, matplotlib and reader caches pointed at `rebaseline/build/` before any import |
| `rebaseline/common.py` | the `stabpen.provenance` block (git head and dirty flag, SHA-256 of every input file, seeds, parameters, command, python/numpy/scipy/mujoco/numba/torch versions), strict JSON, resumable row caches (merged under a file lock, so two processes of one mode keep each other's rows), case and writer-cluster bootstraps |
| `rebaseline/impact.py` | task 1: the register as data (model, faults, classification, rerun pointer and outcome per row), its integrity check, the CSV and the table |
| `rebaseline/sim2j_cards.py` | task 2: the three sensing modes (with the historical firmware contact channel restored at run time for `legacy_exact`), the ET grid, the severe and autowrite blocks, the cards and the paired comparisons |
| `rebaseline/bnib_rerun.py` | task 3: the nib configurations (the attribution ladder, Rev K, the pass's 1.5 mm candidate, study N's balanced candidate), the nonlinear wire law and guide drag per physics step, the measured-contact gate, the reproduction of study B's rows, the summaries and CALC power bands |
| `rebaseline/reach_b1.py` | task 4: the B1 HW1 pens, study F's cases, the aggregation with R's writer bootstrap |
| `rebaseline/page_v2.py` | task 5: the in-memory version-2 fit, the anchored wrapper (patch proposal 6), R's and E's cases, F's gap cases and page sensing check, the v1/v2 cards |
| `rebaseline/report.py`, `rebaseline/evidence.py` | the tables quoted here (`rebaseline/build/doc_tables.md`) and `results/rebaseline/evidence_rows.csv` |
| `rebaseline/run.py` | one command for everything (`--quick` smoke run, `--jobs 1|2`) |
| `rebaseline/tests/test_rebaseline.py` | the tests |

**Results `results/rebaseline/`** (each JSON starts with `stabpen.provenance`): `impact_register.csv`,
`impact_register.json`, `sim2j_cards.json`, `bnib_rerun.json`, `reach_b1.json`, `page_v2.json`, `evidence_rows.csv`.
Per-case rows and caches (git-ignored) are in `rebaseline/build/` (rows, adapted hand paths per sensing mode, the
version-2 case files, logs; `rebaseline/build/sched.py`, the small scheduler that kept at most two of this
study's processes running).

**Commands** (one numerical thread per process, at most two processes; `NUMBA_NUM_THREADS=1 OMP_NUM_THREADS=1
OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1`; do not set `PYTHONNOUSERSITE` on this machine):

| Command (from the repository root) | What | Wall time here |
|---|---|---|
| `python3 -m rebaseline.impact` | task 1: the register (CSV, JSON) | seconds |
| `python3 -m rebaseline.sim2j_cards --mode causal --phase headline` (then `--phase other`, `severe`, `autowrite`) | task 2, causal sensing, 6 writers | 36 + 37 + 15 + 9 min |
| `python3 -m rebaseline.sim2j_cards --mode legacy_flags --phase headline` (then `--phase other`) | task 2, legacy flags on the current code | 33 + 32 min |
| `python3 -m rebaseline.sim2j_cards --mode legacy_exact --phase headline --writers 0,1` | task 2, the reproduction check | 10 min |
| `python3 -m rebaseline.bnib_rerun --config revK_corrected` (and `cand15_corrected`) | task 3, writers 0–5 | 42 + 20 min each |
| `python3 -m rebaseline.bnib_rerun --config <B1_studyB_exact / B1_studyB_now / B1_dec066 / revK_linear / revK_linear_80 / candN_corrected> --writers 0,1` | task 3, the reproduction, the ladder and study N's candidate (`B1_studyB_exact` on writer 0) | 7 / 14 / 14 / 14 / 13 / CANDN_MIN min |
| `python3 -m rebaseline.reach_b1 --run` | task 4 | 17 min |
| `python3 -m rebaseline.page_v2 --gap`, `--sensing`, `--re --notes 0,1,2,3,4`, `--re --notes 5,6,7,8` | task 5 (the reader dominates R's and E's cases: about 2 min each) | 12 / 4 / 75 / 59 min |
| `python3 -m rebaseline.<sim2j_cards / bnib_rerun / reach_b1 / page_v2> --summarise` | the results JSONs from the cached rows | under a minute each |
| `python3 -m rebaseline.report` | `results/rebaseline/evidence_rows.csv` and `rebaseline/build/doc_tables.md` | seconds |
| `python3 -m rebaseline.run [--quick] [--jobs 2]` | everything in order, resumable; `--quick` is a smoke run of every stage that writes only under `rebaseline/build/quick` | about QUICK_MIN min with `--quick` |

Two operational faults, both fixed: the first attempt at task 5 failed on every recorded note (patch proposal 6; the
anchored wrapper was added and the runs repeated), and the causal autowrite block ran twice because its first rows
were overwritten by the severe block, which ran beside it on the same row file (row saves now merge under a file
lock). In all, about 9.7 CPU-hours over 5.2 hours of wall time with at most two of this study's processes at a time (once,
for about two minutes, the scheduler started a third while the smoke run switched stages). The CPU for task 2 was
estimated first from the historical rows' own wall times (12.6 s median per ET run, so about 25–30 min per sensing
mode for the 84 headline runs); the runs took 33–36 min. New files: about 150 MB, all in the git-ignored
`rebaseline/build/` except the results (under 1 MB).

**Tests.** `python3 -m pytest rebaseline/tests -q`: TESTS_PLACEHOLDER
